2Op3QLzMgSY.summary: The first lecture of MIT's 1986 6.001 Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, given by Harold Abelson, introducing Lisp and the idea of computer science as the study of process.
2Op3QLzMgSY.why: Seen as a classic and often the moment programming 'clicks'; commenters praise Abelson's opening that computer science is not about computers.

2V1FtfBDsLU.summary: Rich Hickey's talk at Clojure's tenth anniversary on the kind of programs Clojure is designed for. He argues for situated programs that deal with changing requirements, and for dynamic typing and data over static types.
2V1FtfBDsLU.why: HN's go-to link in typing debates and for talk lists, and several call it their favorite programming talk even for non-Clojure users.

2y5Pv4yN0b0.summary: Java Language Architect Brian Goetz talks at a Clojure conference about the challenges of evolving a mature language like Java while preserving compatibility with existing code and developer expectations. It also gives a look at where the platform is headed.
2y5Pv4yN0b0.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the definitive explanation of why Java evolves cautiously and why compatibility matters in language design.

2pWv7GOvuf0.summary: The first lecture of David Silver's reinforcement learning course, introducing the field and its basic concepts. The course follows the Sutton and Barto textbook.
2pWv7GOvuf0.why: Frequently recommended as an excellent, clear introductory RL course from the lead of AlphaGo, pairing well with Sutton and Barto.

2sjqTHE0zok.summary: A lecture from MIT's Missing Semester course covering version control with git. It builds up git from its data model rather than from commands.
2sjqTHE0zok.why: HN frequently calls it the best single video on git because it teaches the underlying data structures.

2Vrhk5OjBP8.summary: AlphaPhoenix builds a scaled-down version of the Veritasium electricity thought experiment using about a kilometer of wire and an oscilloscope. He measures how the signal actually propagates and explains the result.
2Vrhk5OjBP8.why: HN considers it the best experimental rebuttal and clarification of the Veritasium wire debate, with real measurements.

2tdiKTSdE9Y.summary: Tom Scott investigates the claim that the microwave was invented to heat hamsters, and interviews James Lovelock about freezing and microwave-thawing hamsters in the 1950s. It traces early magnetron uses beyond radar.
2tdiKTSdE9Y.why: HN recommends it as a well-told chase of a weird fact that lands a rare interview with Lovelock at age 101.

2KSahAoOLdU.summary: The first episode of CuriousMarc's series restoring a real Apollo Guidance Computer, led by AGC expert Mike Stewart. They set up a makeshift lab in a Houston hotel room to open up a rare machine owned by a private collector.
2KSahAoOLdU.why: HN people recommend the whole AGC restoration series as a deeply nerdy look at real Apollo-era hardware, including core rope memory.

2AXv49dDQJw.summary: AlphaPhoenix uses a custom high-speed measurement setup to watch voltage waves travel down wires and split at a fork. It answers how electricity knows where to go and how quickly that process happens.
2AXv49dDQJw.why: Praised as the clearest visual explanation of transmission lines, impedance and signal propagation, with several commenters saying it made it all click.

2XLZ4Z8LpEE.summary: CuriousMarc connects a restored 1930 Model 15 Teletype to a Linux machine and uses it as a terminal, after commenters requested it. The video shows the challenges of linking a 5-bit mechanical device to a modern OS.
2XLZ4Z8LpEE.why: HN commenters love it as a vivid demonstration of terminal history, explaining why tools like ed and the tty echo model work the way they do.

2wZ1pCpJUIM.summary: Bryan Cantrill argues that programming languages and platforms reflect core values, and compares languages through that lens, with Rust as a main example. He draws on his experience with Solaris, DTrace and ZFS.
2wZ1pCpJUIM.why: Cited again and again as the framework for discussing languages in terms of values, and how organizational values shape software quality.

2DIl3Hfh9tY.summary: Stanford physicist Leonard Susskind gives a public lecture on the holographic principle, the indestructibility of information and the nature of black holes. It asks whether the world could be a hologram.
2DIl3Hfh9tY.why: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible yet substantive introduction to the holographic principle and black hole information, often when related physics news comes up.

2PdJFbjWHEU.summary: Doug McGuff presents the biochemistry behind high-intensity strength training and the paleo diet, including how the body stores and burns fat. It is a roughly hour-and-a-half full-length lecture.
2PdJFbjWHEU.why: HN recommends it as the theory behind Body by Science, explaining metabolism and why brief intense training works.

2u6HTG8LuXQ.summary: Game Maker's Toolkit examines Nintendo's design approach of starting from a core play mechanic, making it fun, and building around it. Examples include Mario's jump and Luigi's Mansion's vacuum.
2u6HTG8LuXQ.why: HN recommends it as a concise video essay on why Nintendo games feel good and how the company iterates.

2JB1_e5wZmU.summary: Scott Wlaschin shows how statically typed functional languages, using F# examples, can model a business domain so that invalid states cannot be represented. The type system acts almost like an instant unit test at compile time.
2JB1_e5wZmU.why: HN treats it as the canonical, approachable example of domain-driven design with types and 'make invalid states unrepresentable'.

2NBG-sKFaB0.summary: Full gameplay of .kkrieger, a first-person shooter by Farbrausch that fits into a 96KB executable by generating its textures, models and sounds procedurally.
2NBG-sKFaB0.why: HN points to it as the standard example of procedural content generation and extreme size optimization in games.

2S0k12uZR14.summary: Dr. Richard Cook, a physician and patient safety researcher, presents his ideas on how complex systems fail, at Velocity 2012. He argues for designing for resiliency rather than trying to exhaustively handle every failure mode.
2S0k12uZR14.why: HN people recommend it as a must-watch for anyone running complex systems, and some rewatch it regularly to remember its principles.

2gFsOoKAHZg.summary: hbomberguy investigates the modern flat earth movement and why people come to believe it. The video treats the community with a measured, humorous tone and looks at the social causes behind the belief.
2gFsOoKAHZg.why: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining and thoughtful look at flat earthers that frames the belief as a distrust of failing institutions.

2yDCox-qKbk.summary: A short promotional video demonstrating a head-thumping technique that is claimed to relieve tinnitus. Covering the ears and tapping the back of the head is said to silence the ringing temporarily.
2yDCox-qKbk.why: Tinnitus sufferers share it as a free trick that briefly stops the ringing, though not as a cure.

24R8JObNNQ4.summary: Vice founder Shane Smith travels to North Korea, speaking with refugees in South Korea before crossing the DMZ. It is part one of a three-part documentary with rare on-the-ground footage.
24R8JObNNQ4.why: HN commenters recommend it as a rare, eye-opening look inside North Korea, though one notes such tours are staged.

2IT2oAzTcvU.summary: At DEF CON 27, Nina Kollars tells how buying Nespresso capsules on eBay led her to investigate fraudsters reselling goods bought with stolen credit cards. She describes her non-technical tracking and reporting efforts.
2IT2oAzTcvU.why: HN points to it as an entertaining and informative explanation of the economics of reshipping and stolen-card resale scams.

2LyzBoHo5EI.summary: Hans Rosling uses population statistics to explain why the world population will level off rather than grow without limit. He shows that falling child mortality and rising prosperity lead to smaller families.
2LyzBoHo5EI.why: Offered as an approachable, data-driven rebuttal to Malthusian overpopulation fears.

2QrX5jsiico.summary: Travis Kalanick's talk at FailCon 2011 about his earlier failed startups, given as a case study before Uber's rise. It describes lessons from those ventures.
2QrX5jsiico.why: HN commenters recommend it for insight into Kalanick's background and how his past failures shaped his mindset at Uber.

24OXzIRIiMQ.summary: Audio clips of the intro and technology quotes from the 1999 strategy game Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri, in male and female voices, covering techs 0 through 24.
24OXzIRIiMQ.why: HN fans share it as a way to hear the game's philosophical, sci-fi quotes in sequence.

2EWejmkKlxs.summary: Chandler Carruth shows how to squeeze more performance out of already-optimized C++ code, covering how the CPU executes it. The talk goes into pipelining, branch prediction and speculative execution using benchmarks.
2EWejmkKlxs.why: Recommended as the best presentation on how modern CPUs run code, and why speculative execution matters for performance.

2FMBSblpcrc.summary: A short TEDx talk by Joe Smith teaching how to dry your hands with a single paper towel. It shows a simple technique for cutting waste.
2FMBSblpcrc.why: HN treats it as a tiny practical life hack some adopt for good, while others mock it as peak TED.

2KZb2_vcNTg.summary: Veritasium asks people where a tree's mass comes from, then explains that most of a dry tree's mass originates from carbon dioxide in the air. It combines street interviews with a short explanation of photosynthesis.
2KZb2_vcNTg.why: HN uses it as the go-to demonstration of how unintuitive mass conservation is, especially in weight loss and burning threads.

2R07FL1wVo4.summary: A presentation by Janice Stanger arguing that protein is overhyped and that excess or the wrong kinds of protein are harmful. It promotes a whole-foods, plant-based diet.
2R07FL1wVo4.why: A few commenters cite it as a starting point for the claim that excess protein is harmful, though the claims are one-sided advocacy.

2SuvO4Gi7uY.summary: Martin Donald explains the Wave Function Collapse algorithm using Sudoku-like constraint solving and shows how he implemented it with Blender and Godot. It links demos and reference articles.
2SuvO4Gi7uY.why: Commenters recommend it as the clearest way to understand WFC, especially in threads about Townscaper and tiled content generation.

2THVvshvq0Q.summary: An Every Frame a Painting video essay on Michael Bay's style, 'Bayhem', covering his camera movement, composition, color and editing. It argues that even if you dislike his films, they teach something about visual perception.
2THVvshvq0Q.why: HN recommends it as a short, well-produced and eye-opening piece of film analysis.

2aCOyOvOw5c.summary: Footage from a camera on a Space Shuttle solid rocket booster from liftoff through descent, with audio enhanced by Skywalker Sound from the original camera microphones. The sound is real, not foley.
2aCOyOvOw5c.why: HN recommends it for its raw, mostly natural audio and for conveying the speeds and violence of a shuttle launch and booster descent.

2nBPN-MKefA.summary: An animated documentary by Paul Grignon explaining how modern money is created through bank lending as debt. This is a combined upload of the revised 2009 edition.
2nBPN-MKefA.why: HN commenters recommend it as a cartoonish but thorough explanation of the monetary system, though some critics dispute its claims.

2zvjW9arAZ0.summary: Bassist Victor Wooten argues that music should be learned the way children learn their first language: by immersion and play, without early correction or rigid academic instruction. He draws on how babies pick up speech from the people around them.
2zvjW9arAZ0.why: HN commenters point to it when discussing how to teach children or beginners, as a language-like alternative to formal instruction.

21j_OCNLuYg.summary: Thai farmer Jon Jandai talks about leaving Bangkok to farm and build his own house, arguing that food, shelter, clothing and medicine are easy to provide and that modern life is made needlessly complicated. He founded the Pun Pun Center for Self-reliance.
21j_OCNLuYg.why: HN recommends it as a thoughtful counterpoint to the pursuit of complicated, consumption-driven lives.

2A2NY29iQdI.summary: Engineer Stuff Made Here builds two new supposedly unpickable locks with different designs and sends them to the Lock Picking Lawyer to see whether they can be defeated. The video covers the novel anti-picking mechanisms.
2A2NY29iQdI.why: HN people recommend it, along with the Lock Picking Lawyer's response, as an engaging look at lock design and how clever mechanisms get bypassed.

2AecAXinars.summary: DIY Perks builds a webcam mod using a two-way mirror in a box so the camera sits behind the screen image. This allows real eye contact on video calls.
2AecAXinars.why: Whenever eye contact in video calls comes up, commenters point to this as the cheap homemade teleprompter-style solution.

2AnbYNudAyM.summary: Razor 1911's eponymous demo celebrating 40 years of the group, which won first place at the Revision 2026 demo competition and the public's choice award. It is a retrospective of keygen and warez scene culture with chiptune music.
2AnbYNudAyM.why: HN commenters point to it as an impressive showpiece of the demoscene and a nostalgic career retrospective of a legendary group.

2JAOTJxYqh8.summary: Mark Rober digs into bed bugs, testing popular beliefs about where they come from and how to get rid of them. It mixes entertaining experiments with research-based advice on what works and what does not.
2JAOTJxYqh8.why: HN commenters point to it as a fun, research-grounded explainer whenever bed bug threads come up.

2OSrvzNW9FE.summary: A short Veritasium video showing how far a backspinning basketball would travel dropped off a dam. It demonstrates the Magnus effect and links to Flettner rotor ships and aircraft.
2OSrvzNW9FE.why: HN uses it as a quick, clear demonstration of the Magnus effect behind spinning-cylinder ships and planes.

2xcZS7arcgk.summary: Geoff Lawton documents a permaculture project that turned barren Jordanian desert into green, productive land. It covers the techniques he used.
2xcZS7arcgk.why: Cited in climate and carbon-removal threads as an inspiring example of re-greening deserts.

29u_FejNuks.summary: The Townsends channel shows how to make mushroom ketchup, a popular 18th-century sauce, in period style. It includes the history and a recipe and links to a blog post on whether George Washington used ketchup.
29u_FejNuks.why: HN commenters who have cooked it recommend it as a reliable, delicious recipe and a good historical explanation of pre-tomato ketchup.

2WoDQBhJCVQ.summary: A one-minute clip from James Burke's 1978 BBC series Connections in which he walks past a Saturn V rocket and a timed take-off happens behind him in a single shot, with no green screen.
2WoDQBhJCVQ.why: Held up as an iconic, perfectly timed piece of television whenever Burke or Connections comes up.

2-oBNh0UkQc.summary: A demonstration of SymbOS, a multitasking operating system for 8-bit Z80 machines, running on a real MSX turboR with an MP3MSX card and a CF IDE interface. It shows the OS playing audio and running a graphical desktop on very old hardware, captured from the real machine and not an emulator.
2-oBNh0UkQc.why: HN points to it as a vivid showcase of how much a modern-feeling GUI OS can do on slow 8-bit hardware.

21EiKfQYZXc.summary: Andrew Ng speaks at the Stanford MSx Future Forum about how AI is transforming industry after industry, comparing its impact to electricity. The talk also touches on evil-AI worries, jobs and basic income.
21EiKfQYZXc.why: Recommended as a broad, practical view of AI's near-term impact from a leading practitioner, with his argument that worrying about evil AI is premature.

23X14HS4gLk.summary: A 1947 US military film that deconstructs how the Nazi regime used divisive propaganda and prejudice to split and control a population. It teaches viewers to recognise demagoguery tactics.
23X14HS4gLk.why: Shared in political threads as a timeless warning about divisive manipulation and demagogues.

29RkHH-psrY.summary: A Computer History Museum oral history interview with Dave Cutler, covering his youth, early work on operating systems at DuPont and Digital Equipment, and his path toward VMS and Windows NT. This is part one of a long-form interview.
29RkHH-psrY.why: Recommended as a rare long-form interview with a legendary operating system designer, though some find it light on technical detail.

2BdBfsXbST8.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Donald Knuth about algorithms, complexity, The Art of Computer Programming, and his work habits. The conversation covers his approach to verifying algorithms and how he organises his time.
2BdBfsXbST8.why: Cited as an excellent look at Knuth's thinking and working style, and as a likely source for quotes about his habits.

2Ex8EEv-WPs.summary: Yehuda Katz's Railsberry 2012 talk on why Rails is hard to learn and use. He explains that the framework's many features reflect real complexity in web applications that newcomers do not yet see.
2Ex8EEv-WPs.why: Recommended to people who call Rails bloated, as an argument that its size comes from features you eventually need.

2Q26XIKtwXQ.summary: A short CNN clip of Peter Thiel telling Google chairman Eric Schmidt that Google has huge cash reserves and does not know how to invest them. Thiel argues this signals a lack of innovation.
2Q26XIKtwXQ.why: HN reaches for it whenever big tech cash hoarding, buybacks or stagnating innovation come up.

2SdGkkp1aq8.summary: Robotic Liberation by PWP is a music video demo performed entirely by an unexpanded Commodore VIC-20 and a 1541 disk drive, using only a few kilobytes of RAM and a 16 KB disk. It uses demoscene effects to tell a story.
2SdGkkp1aq8.why: HN recommends it as a showcase of what skilled demoscene programmers can squeeze out of extremely limited hardware.

2U9WMftV40c.summary: Rick Roderick's 1993 lecture on Baudrillard, the last in his series The Self Under Siege. It covers hyperreality, simulation and what Baudrillard calls fatal strategies.
2U9WMftV40c.why: Recommended as a much easier way into Baudrillard's ideas than reading his own writing.

2lisQQmWQkY.summary: A 2018 tutorial explaining uBlock Origin's advanced user mode, including how to block scripts and use the dynamic filtering settings. It positions the extension as a replacement for tools like uMatrix.
2lisQQmWQkY.why: HN points newcomers to it as the thing to watch before tackling uBlock Origin's advanced mode and filter syntax.

2qsmF8HHskg.summary: A short demo of SEdit, the structure editor for Interlisp-D on Xerox Lisp machines in the 1980s, which edits code as trees rather than text.
2qsmF8HHskg.why: Linked as the clearest view of the legendary structural editor in threads about Lisp environments and structure editing.

2vuMzGhc1cg.summary: A 43-minute skeptical critique arguing that Starlink fails to live up to its promises, covering satellite lifespan, costs, bandwidth and viability. The creator later added an update about FCC grant requirements.
2vuMzGhc1cg.why: A few commenters recommend it as a skeptical take on Starlink economics, though others see it as dishonest.

2wq9x2QcZN0.summary: Lex Fridman interviews mathematician and economist Eric Weinstein about science, mathematics, and society. The conversation ranges across physics, academia, AI and job displacement.
2wq9x2QcZN0.why: HN refers to it for Weinstein's views on advanced math and physics and academia's problems, though some find him a bit kooky.

2B-XwPjn9YY.summary: A restored recording of Steve Jobs unveiling the original Macintosh in 1984, including the moment it is taken out of its bag and speaks. The upload comes from the team that rediscovered and restored the lost footage.
2B-XwPjn9YY.why: HN commenters cite it as the source for the talking-Macintosh introduction, usually in threads about speech synthesis and audio.

2BIx2x-Q2fE.summary: Cliff Stoll shows and explains his two Friden EC-132 electronic calculators for Numberphile. The video covers how these early machines worked, including their unusual acoustic delay line memory.
2BIx2x-Q2fE.why: It is the go-to visual explanation of delay-line memory and early electronic calculators whenever the topic comes up.

2JM2oImb9Qg.summary: Numberphile's James Grime discusses highly composite numbers, nicknamed anti-primes, which have more factors than any smaller number, using 5040 as the central example. It touches on Plato and Ramanujan.
2JM2oImb9Qg.why: HN points to it whenever highly divisible numbers matter, such as sharding, base 12, time units and music.

2o8MDCIlOEk.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog tears down an Esinomed Infoview medical tablet computer built around an 800MHz AMD Geode board, exposing extremely shoddy construction and design.
2o8MDCIlOEk.why: HN calls it a famous, hilarious teardown and a go-to example of terrible hardware quality.

2z5A-COlDPk.summary: Technology Connections explains why car turn signals appear to drift out of sync at stoplights and how thermal and other flasher designs work. It also covers how synchronization could be achieved.
2z5A-COlDPk.why: Referenced as a typical example of the channel's hacker-eye view of everyday technology, and for its flasher explanation.

21qPOReu4FI.summary: Andrej Bauer's IAS talk introduces constructive mathematics and what it feels like to do mathematics without excluded middle. It is framed as a tour for classical mathematicians.
21qPOReu4FI.why: Pointed to as a well-done introduction to constructive mathematics when it comes up in logic and proof assistant threads.

2BO83Ig-E8E.summary: Two Australian YouTubers travel to North Korea and get a haircut while examining how Western media sensationalizes stories about the country.
2BO83Ig-E8E.why: Cited as a satirical counterpoint to Western news claims about North Korea, including debunking the compulsory haircut myth.

2D9ExVc0G10.summary: Alex Ionescu's OffensiveCon 2019 keynote on how reverse engineering is done on Windows without conventional reversing. It covers legal ways to obtain names of variables, exported functions and structures.
2D9ExVc0G10.why: Cited in ReactOS threads as an authoritative account of how Windows reverse engineering works and as a rebuttal to claims about ReactOS.

2PCb9mnrU1g.summary: A VICE interview with Martin Shkreli about the 5000 percent price hike on a drug for AIDS-related infections and his role as the world's villain.
2PCb9mnrU1g.why: HN refers to it as a chance to hear Shkreli's own side of the drug pricing story, including his claim that it is common practice.

2Pn1RVZu-24.summary: A one-minute clip of comedian Bill Burr answering whether women can be funny at the Just For Laughs festival.
2Pn1RVZu-24.why: HN links it as a quotable rant to illustrate points about bias and outsiders in unrelated threads.

2RQrKP9a0XE.summary: A short BicycleDutch episode showing Vredenburg in Utrecht, the busiest cycle path in the Netherlands, with about 37,000 cyclists passing on a working day.
2RQrKP9a0XE.why: HN uses it as visual evidence that cycling can move huge numbers of commuters in little space.

2YoPoNx3L5E.summary: An AdaCore webinar in which NVIDIA engineers explain why and how they adopted Ada and SPARK for security-critical firmware. It covers the business case and the engineering experience of the transition.
2YoPoNx3L5E.why: HN cites it in Rust-versus-C++ and Ada discussions as a real industrial case of choosing SPARK for safer embedded code.

2Z43y94Dfzk.summary: Archival footage of Larry Tesler demonstrating Gypsy, the modeless text editor he and Tim Mott built at Xerox PARC, running on the Computer History Museum's restored Alto. It is a long hands-on walkthrough of one of the earliest graphical document editors.
2Z43y94Dfzk.why: Referenced in discussions of early GUIs and Alto history as a rare first-hand demonstration by the creator.

2b3ttqYDwF0.summary: Stanford futurist Tony Seba argues that electric vehicles, battery storage, solar and autonomous vehicles form a 10x exponential disruption that will make fossil fuels obsolete within about a decade. It draws on his Clean Disruption book.
2b3ttqYDwF0.why: HN commenters cite it as a big-picture case for exponential solar and EV adoption, usually with caveats about whether his predictions will hold.

2f2kGHcdJYU.summary: A two-minute clip from the film Margin Call in which Will Emerson talks about how banks and traders operate and why they stay necessary. The uploader posted it because they agree with the speech.
2f2kGHcdJYU.why: HN cites it as a compact explanation of the housing crash and of institutions keeping their fingers on the scales.

2guvwQvElA8.summary: LockPickingLawyer shows a Sentry fire safe being cut in half with a saw in a few minutes. It is a short demonstration that these safes offer little protection against a determined thief.
2guvwQvElA8.why: Used to illustrate that fire safes protect against fire and not theft, and that brute force often defeats low-security containers.

2hf9yN-oBV4.summary: The Thought Emporium shows how they engineered a yeast strain to produce real spider silk, after more than two years of lab work and many failures. The video explains the genetic engineering process behind it.
2hf9yN-oBV4.why: HN commenters cite it as proof that cutting-edge biotech is becoming accessible to home labs, much like computing in the 1980s.

2k8fHR9jKVM.summary: A two-minute BBC Horizon clip demonstrating the McGurk effect, where what you see of a speaker's mouth changes the sound you hear.
2k8fHR9jKVM.why: Recommended as a quick demo of vision overriding hearing, and cited as an example of perception producing confident wrong answers.

2qv3fcXW1mg.summary: Google engineers describe Google's internal build system, a unified, language-agnostic system used across the company. It was presented as a 2012 NYC tech talk.
2qv3fcXW1mg.why: Referenced as a rare public description of how Google builds software, from which tools like Bazel descend.

20TAkcy3aBY.summary: Jon Stewart on The Daily Show satirizes the AI industry's promises of a better future while it builds technology to replace workers. It mocks executives and AI hype.
20TAkcy3aBY.why: Cited in AI threads as a comedic take on corporate AI hype and executives wanting to cut headcount.

21EYKqUsPfg.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews Richard Sutton, reinforcement learning pioneer, Turing Award winner and author of The Bitter Lesson. Sutton argues LLMs are a dead end because they cannot learn on the job, and that continual learning from experience will require a new architecture.
21EYKqUsPfg.why: HN commenters cite it as the serious skeptic's case against LLMs reaching general intelligence, usually in debates about whether scaling is enough.

22wlLy7hKP4.summary: The keynote launch video for the Rabbit r1 handheld AI device, presenting its assistant and a teachable mode for agents. It is a product announcement with live-style demos.
22wlLy7hKP4.why: HN mostly cites it as an example of a misleading or faked product demo, with a few pointing to its teachable-mode segment.

23vjWtUpItk.summary: Linus Tech Tips argues that big air coolers beat AIO liquid coolers for most PCs. They compare quietness and temperatures, using the Noctua NH-U12A as the example.
23vjWtUpItk.why: HN cites it as evidence that a good air cooler matches pricier liquid cooling, so water cooling is often unnecessary.

24q80ReMyq0.summary: Smarter Every Day films a bullet hitting a Prince Rupert's drop with a high-speed camera at 150,000 fps. It shows how the glass drop's tough head and fragile tail behave on impact.
24q80ReMyq0.why: HN cites it as the go-to high-speed footage whenever Prince Rupert's drops come up.

24srQXX81Oc.summary: A short Bookeen R&D demo showing smooth H.264 video playback on a Pearl E Ink panel, driven by a TI OMAP3621 chip and custom controller software.
24srQXX81Oc.why: HN cites it as proof that e-ink screens can reach video frame rates, in threads about fast e-ink refresh and displays.

25J3u3P-HHg.summary: An SNL sketch in which Nick Burns, the condescending IT guy, trains a new tech support hire to mock users over simple computer problems.
25J3u3P-HHg.why: Used as shorthand for the arrogant, dismissive tech support person in jokes and comparisons.

25ZuKkbHdqM.summary: Jay Leno drives the Tesla Cybertruck with Elon Musk, who talks about the design, including the stainless steel body and bulletproof doors, and Leno demos the roll-up bed cover.
25ZuKkbHdqM.why: Cited as a primary source for what Musk said about the Cybertruck's design goals and for its huge view count.

25hLohVZdME.summary: Terry Davis, author of TempleOS, demonstrates his SimStructure physics simulator and builds a PID controller using math from Numerical Recipes in C. The description notes PID controllers are used in everything from rockets to espresso machines.
25hLohVZdME.why: HN links it with timestamps as an early, hands-on demo of control theory and as a curiosity from Davis's work.

26ZDB9h7BLY.summary: The classic Monty Python Four Yorkshiremen sketch from Live at the Hollywood Bowl, in which four men try to outdo each other with exaggerated tales of childhood hardship.
26ZDB9h7BLY.why: Used as a joke reference when someone claims to have had it harder than others.

2C-zWrhFqpM.summary: Noam Chomsky speaks at Google Cambridge in 2017 about his political development and the control of information and media. It is a wide-ranging talk with audience discussion.
2C-zWrhFqpM.why: HN mostly links it as background in political arguments or for a memorable moment, rather than as a recommendation.

2HMPRXstSvQ.summary: A one-minute clip from a 2016 Toronto conference in which Geoff Hinton comments on deep learning and radiology. He suggests radiologists should stop being trained because machines would soon read scans better.
2HMPRXstSvQ.why: HN uses it as a famous example of an overconfident AI prediction that turned out wrong, since radiologists remain in demand.

2HZs-v0PR44.summary: A short Middle East Eye news clip of Joe Biden telling Israeli President Isaac Herzog that if there were not an Israel, the US would have to invent one. The description notes a similar remark from 1986.
2HZs-v0PR44.why: Posted as a reference clip in geopolitical threads about Israel and US policy, not as a recommendation.

2Ntp6BqhSng.summary: A vlogbrothers video tracing how the claim that people eat a credit card of plastic every week spread. It walks through the funded talking point, the misleading amplification, and the peer review that missed it.
2Ntp6BqhSng.why: Linked in microplastics and recycling threads as a debunking of a viral statistic.

2S-WJN3L5eo.summary: A Jubilee debate-format video in which progressive commentator Mehdi Hasan faces twenty far-right conservatives. It covers contentious political topics in a confrontational discussion.
2S-WJN3L5eo.why: HN mentions mostly use it as an example of extreme views or to criticize participants in political threads, not as a recommendation.

2S2qtGisT34.summary: A CNN report in which Nima Elbagir witnesses migrants being auctioned as slaves at a property outside Tripoli, Libya.
